investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T22:33–22:40Z because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are fully exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, and the pod's node affinity/selector rules prevent scheduling on the other 4 nodes. Because the pod remained Unschedulable for the full probe window (~126–146 s), the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so zero required evidence fields were written and all contract assertions failed. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to this observability eval.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Swarm Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Three Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster had only 2 nodes eligible for kata peer-pod VMs, both of which reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no VM could be scheduled, the eval probe's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-infrastructure failure localized to the Kubernetes swarm backing remote agent provisioning; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing remote agent VM provisioning exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the remote-agent pod affinity/selector. With 0 schedulable nodes and preemption unable to free capacity, every pod submitted by the eval probe remained Unschedulable for the full timeout window (~126–148 s), causing all three remote-agent checks to fail before any agent was created or any runtime response was obtained. The root cause is resource exhaustion of the kata peer-pod VM slot on the eligible node pool, not an application code defect.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior eval run consumed all available peer-pod VM quota, leaving no capacity for the eval probe pods. Supported by all three sibling checks failing with the same scheduler message.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, meaning the effective schedulable pool is permanently constrained to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes have a low VM slot limit, any concurrent load will exhaust capacity. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — VM slot limit set too low on the eligible node pool: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit per node may be under-provisioned relative to the number of concurrent eval or user workloads expected. Supported by 'No preemption victims found' indicating no lower-priority pods exist to evict.

Lower confidence — a transient spike in remote agent usage by other workloads at the time of the eval run (2026-07-17T22:35–22:40Z) temporarily exhausted capacity that would otherwise be available. No traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm or deny this.
